assessments.summary: Under the accepted 30-row system and posterior-measure reduction, the argument establishes the binary-input receiver-curve modulus, compactness and finite-output uniform density of generalized receiver curves, exact finite-grid matching with the stated cardinality and error bounds, preservation of already reflected pairs on reflection-closed grids, and stability of all 30 row right sides with the audited coefficients and universal bound. It consequently establishes feasibility for the explicitly relaxed approximating systems and persistence of strictly feasible witnesses under sufficiently fine approximations.
scopeQualifications: Validity is premise-bound to the accepted 30-row system from e3c1036ca607539a5ebcddf3058e6014ac5c1cd9, including its external theorem premise.
The approximation result preserves an already reflected receiver pair on a reflection-closed grid; it does not symmetrize arbitrary pairs or establish reflected optimality.
Feasibility is established under explicit row relaxations; no unrelaxed optimized-value convergence is proved.
No exact full-functional cardinality bound, minimax interchange, numerical capacity improvement, or exact sum-capacity is established.

Computational attestations check the encoded dependency list, 30-row coefficient algebra, global coefficient bound, and tested grid formulas; the entropy, compactness, Carathéodory, and arbitrary-grid arguments are established mathematically rather than by those computations.
